title: Design System: Rubén Sánchez Corcuera · Courses

headline.purpose: Course title on a cover; weight 500 when forthcoming.

lede.purpose: Intro sentence, max 46ch; also the email link size.

link.purpose: Course part links; language switch at 14px.

label.purpose: Cover spine: language, year or Forthcoming.

shadows.name: volume-rest
shadows.purpose: Published cover at rest: spine strip, contact shadow, long drop.

shadows.name: volume-lifted
shadows.purpose: Published cover on hover, with translateY(-6px) rotate(-.6deg).

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Cover lift and every drawing replay.

motion.name: draw
motion.value: 0.7s default, 1-1.4s for fitted curves and walks
motion.purpose: Stroke drawn via dashoffset, staggered by --d.

motion.name: pop
motion.purpose: Points and numerals scale in from 0.2.

motion.name: grow
motion.purpose: Histogram bars scale up from the baseline.

motion.name: replay-stagger
motion.purpose: First-view replay order across the shelf, at 60% visibility.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Finished drawing shown, no transitions or replays.

narrative.overview:
Every course is a volume in one series, and the catalog is the shelf they stand on. A published course is a solid-colour book cover in its own identity colour, with a white line drawing of its subject; a course in preparation is the same volume left as a grey outline. The ground is a cool, quiet grey so the covers carry all the colour on the page.

Density is low and the page is short: a condensed display title, one lede, four covers, a colophon. Type does the structural work (Archivo condensed for anything that names a thing, Source Sans 3 for anything read), and depth exists only where a physical book would have it. The course colours are not decoration of this page; they are each course's identity and travel with it to its own Quarto site.
keyCharacteristics: One solid identity colour per published course, used as the whole cover, never as an accent sprinkle.
Cool grey ground and near-black ink; no other hues outside the course set.
Condensed Archivo at heavy weight for names; Source Sans 3 for reading.
White single-weight line drawings of each subject, which replay how they were drawn.
Forthcoming volumes are grey outlines: no colour, no links, no motion.

rules.name: The One Course, One Colour Rule
rules.body: Each course owns exactly one colour, used as its full cover here and as its identity on its course site. A new course gets a new hue of similar depth (white text must pass AA on it); it never borrows another course's colour or a tint of one.

rules.name: The Earned Colour Rule
rules.body: A course shows its colour only once it is published. Until then its cover is a 1.5px Hairline outline with Muted Slate type and a Pencil Grey drawing.

rules.name: The Spine Type Rule
rules.body: Archivo names (titles, brand, spine, drawing numerals); Source Sans 3 explains. Never set reading text in Archivo or a title in Source Sans 3.

rules.name: The Only Books Have Depth Rule
rules.body: Shadows belong to covers. Header, links, colophon and forthcoming outlines stay flat.

dos: Do give each published course its full cover in its own identity colour, with all type and line work in Paper White.
Do draw a course's subject in single-weight white strokes on a 200 by 116 canvas, and make its replay show how the result is reached, ending on the finished drawing.
Do keep forthcoming courses as Hairline outlines with Pencil Grey drawings, no links, no motion.
Do set names in condensed heavy Archivo and reading text in Source Sans 3.
Do keep the email link as the one Deusto Blue element outside a cover.
donts: Don't put a course colour on a course that is not published, or reuse one course's colour for another.
Don't add shadows to anything other than a published cover.
Don't add a generic icon-card grid; a course is a volume, not a card with an icon.
Don't use official University of Deusto branding or marks; the site is personal and says so.
